description: Known issues and error patterns for ROSA HCP test automation

patterns.description: AWS CloudFormation stack deletion failure detected during post-deletion verification
symptoms: Orphaned AWS resources (VPC, SGs, NAT gateways)
Security group dependencies blocking VPC deletion
common_causes: ROSA-created security groups (e.g. *-vpce-private-router) not managed by CloudFormation
VPC endpoint ENI attachments not cleaned up
Resources created outside CloudFormation blocking stack deletion

patterns.pattern: (?i)(?:not authorized to access AWS Account|rosa create ocm-role|CLUSTERS-MGMT-403)
patterns.description: OCM role is not linked to the AWS account. The ROSA organization cannot create or manage clusters in this AWS account.
symptoms: Organization not authorized to access AWS Account
common_causes: OCM role was deleted from AWS but still referenced in OCM
OCM role was never created for this AWS account
OCM role was unlinked from the organization
resolution_steps: 1. Check if an OCM role exists: aws iam list-roles --query 'Roles[?contains(RoleName, `OCM-Role`)]'
2. If the role exists but is unlinked: rosa link ocm-role --role-arn <role-arn>
3. If the role doesn't exist: rosa unlink ocm-role (to clear stale reference), then rosa create ocm-role --admin --mode auto --yes
4. IMPORTANT: Never delete or modify roles with 'mv' prefix — those belong to other developers

patterns.description: CAPI/CAPA controllers not installed or running

common_causes: Too many API calls in short period

patterns.description: ROSAControlPlane stuck in deletion state due to finalizers or AWS resource cleanup
symptoms: ROSAControlPlane has deletionTimestamp but won't delete
ROSA cluster still deprovisioning in AWS
common_causes: ROSA cluster still deprovisioning in AWS
Controller unable to clean up resources

patterns.description: ROSANetwork stuck in deletion state due to finalizers or VPC dependencies
symptoms: ROSANetwork has deletionTimestamp but won't delete
VPC or CloudFormation stack still exists
common_causes: Controller unable to clean up resources

patterns.description: ROSARoleConfig stuck in deletion state due to finalizers or IAM cleanup
symptoms: ROSARoleConfig has deletionTimestamp but won't delete
IAM roles still being cleaned up
common_causes: Controller unable to clean up resources

patterns.description: VPC deletion failure due to orphaned dependencies
symptoms: VPC has dependencies and cannot be deleted
ROSANetwork stuck waiting for VPC deletion

patterns.pattern: (?i)(?:Invalid number of min replicas.*multiple of the private subnets|CLUSTERS-MGMT-400.*replicas.*subnets|compute nodes.*multiple of.*subnets)
patterns.description: MachinePool replica count is not a multiple of the number of availability zones (private subnets). ROSA requires replicas to be evenly distributed across AZs.
symptoms: Invalid number of min replicas error
Cluster retrying for 30+ minutes then timing out
common_causes: Template hardcodes minReplicas=1 or replicas=2 but cluster has 2 or 3 AZs
Availability zone count changed without updating replica count
MachinePool spec doesn't derive replicas from AZ count
resolution_steps: 1. Check AZ count: oc get rosacontrolplane <name> -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{.spec.availabilityZones}'
2. Patch MachinePool replicas to match AZ count: oc patch machinepool <name> -n <ns> --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"replicas":<az_count>}}'
3. Patch autoscaling minReplicas: oc patch rosacontrolplane <name> -n <ns> --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"defaultMachinePoolSpec":{"autoscaling":{"minReplicas":<az_count>}}}}'
4. For future provisions, ensure templates derive replicas from availability_zones_list | length

patterns.description: ROSA/OCM worker-preflight instance profile leak. During cluster provisioning, the ROSA service creates rosa-service-managed-staging-*-<cluster>-worker-preflight instance profiles for each reconciliation attempt. If the control plane reconciliation loops rapidly (e.g., due to a stuck or failing provision), hundreds of empty instance profiles accumulate and are never cleaned up. AWS account limit is 1,000.
symptoms: Instance profile count approaching or at 1,000
Profiles created in rapid succession (seconds apart) during a single provisioning attempt
New cluster provisioning fails with LimitExceeded
common_causes: ROSA service creates a new worker-preflight instance profile on each control plane reconciliation loop
Cluster stuck in reconciliation (e.g., ROSAControlPlane not reaching Ready) causes rapid profile creation
ROSA service does not clean up preflight instance profiles after use or on failure
Known upstream ROSA/OCM bug — profiles are created but never garbage-collected
resolution_steps: 1. Identify the cluster prefix: aws iam list-instance-profiles --query 'InstanceProfiles[*].InstanceProfileName' | grep worker-preflight | sed 's/.*-\([a-z]*\)-worker-preflight/\1/' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
2. Verify profiles are empty (no attached roles): aws iam list-instance-profiles --query 'InstanceProfiles[?contains(InstanceProfileName, `<cluster>-worker-preflight`)].[InstanceProfileName,Roles]'

3. Bulk delete: aws iam list-instance-profiles --query 'InstanceProfiles[?contains(InstanceProfileName, `<cluster>-worker-preflight`)].InstanceProfileName' --output text | tr '\t' '\n' | xargs -P10 -I{} aws iam delete-instance-profile --instance-profile-name {}
4. File upstream bug with ROSA/OCM team for missing garbage collection of preflight instance profiles

patterns.description: OCM reports 'failed to build initial node pools for cluster' — control plane provisions successfully but default worker node pool fails to initialize. OCM marks cluster as error state with provision error code OCM5001. CAPA controller has no recovery path once OCM sets error state.
symptoms: Cluster state: error with OCM5001 provision error code
ROSAControlPlaneReady: False with reason 'error' and message 'OCM5001'
Install logs show control plane reached 'available' state
failureMessage: 'ROSA with HCP cluster provision has failed'
common_causes: Transient AWS capacity issues in selected availability zones
Timing issues in OCM internal node pool orchestration
Subnet or NAT gateway connectivity problems (rare — verify network health)
Worker IAM role trust policy misconfiguration (rare — verify roles)
resolution_steps: 1. Verify network health: oc get rosanetwork <name>-network -n <ns> — confirm ROSANetworkReady: True
2. Verify roles: oc get rosaroleconfig <name>-roles -n <ns> — confirm ROSARoleConfigReady: True
3. Check install logs: rosa logs install -c <ocm-id> — confirm control plane reached 'available'
4. If network and roles are healthy, this is a transient OCM failure — delete and reprovision
5. The cluster spec, network, and roles can be reused on retry
patterns.adjustment_reason: First occurrence — transient failure observed on ttt-422-test (4.22.4, stable channel)
